question.text: Hariyali Foundation (forest-conservation NPO) received INR 3 lakh of anonymous donations during the year. Total donations for the year were INR 40 lakh. Under Section 115BBI, what is the tax liability on the anonymous donations?

answer.text: INR 90,000 — the entire INR 3 lakh is taxed at 30% flat
INR 0 — fully exempt because INR 3 lakh is within 5% of total donations
INR 30,000 — tax at 30% on INR 1 lakh (only the amount above 5% of total donations)
INR 60,000 — tax at 20% on the full anonymous donation amount

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 115BBI taxes anonymous donations at 30% flat to the extent they exceed the HIGHER of (a) INR 1 lakh or (b) 5% of total donations. 5% of INR 40 lakh = INR 2 lakh. Higher of 1 lakh and 2 lakh = INR 2 lakh threshold. Anonymous donations above threshold = INR 3 lakh - INR 2 lakh = INR 1 lakh. Tax = 30% x INR 1 lakh = INR 30,000. The Trap: Taxing the full INR 3 lakh ignores the threshold carve-out. Treating the whole amount as exempt misses the 115BBI trigger. The 20% rate is fabricated; the statutory rate is 30%. Cross-Exam Context: V-A / X-A/X-B touch 115BBI when explaining why receipts-side anti-abuse rules can reduce the NPO's net spend on objectives. XXIII asks the SIA to compute this correctly when reconciling application-of-income. Assessor's Pro-Tip: In your SAS-100 assurance, flag 115BBI tax as a 'leakage' line item when computing the effective application ratio — it reduces the pot available for mission spend even though the NPO booked the receipt as 'donation'.
